title: Bitcoin & Gold CMAs — follow-up deck (point-by-point behind the update email)
desc: 21 slides mirroring the update email's outline: lit review (with the papers/shops map), driver translation, the monthly model with the mean-reversion test, the intercept as a structural-growth identity (~6%/yr = asset growth minus gold supply growth) with the 20-year share cycle, the dollar-leg and rate-leg open questions, left-tail hedging (drawdown chart + rolling 20y real returns with equity-bottom-quartile windows highlighted), Bitcoin's driver inconstancy vs the gold control, and the share-of-gold + survival-branch approach. Appendix: other frequencies, walk-forward OOS, inflation-swap cross-check, top-6 official holders.

title: Bitcoin has no sustainable drivers — rolling correlations, R², and subsample betas (chartpack)
desc: Six pages, monthly 2011-2026: rolling 12m/24m correlations and univariate R-sq of BTC vs twelve candidate drivers (S&P, gold, DXY, real rates, US & world M2, MOVE, Nasdaq, VIX, Fed balance sheet, active addresses, hashrate). Every exogenous driver wanders across zero at both windows; the only persistent correlates - equity beta and BTC's own network activity - are risk appetite and reflexivity, not forecastable fundamentals. Gold run through the identical battery as the control (its DXY/real-rate spine holds). Subsample beta tables 2011-14/15-18/19-21/22-25.

title: The Dollar Leg of the Gold Model — DXY vs Fed indices vs custom gold-buyer baskets
desc: Open design question for review: a trade-weighted dollar represents neither the marginal buyer/seller of gold nor the average holder. Nine USD measures raced on monthly gold returns 1990-2026: the Fed float-weighted major index encompasses DXY; demand-weighted baskets fail mechanically (managed currencies carry weight, no return variance); the official-holder basket is Euro-heavy and adds nothing. The Asia-weighted private-holder basket (INR 31/CNY 30 ~ the marginal buyer) is the best single measure since 2022 (R-sq .304) and clears |t|>2 in that window only - a monitored regime signal, not yet a durable trend (10y rolling t = -1.9).

title: Gold through every major drawdown — S&P, small-cap, 60/40, and Treasury bears (chartpack)
desc: Four pages, monthly 1970-2025: each index's drawdown-from-peak with gold's cumulative return through the episode on the same axis, every episode labeled with its economic story (oil embargo, Volcker, GFC, COVID, 2022 rate shock). Equity drawdowns >10%, small-cap >15%, 60/40 >10%, 10y Treasury >8% - the Treasury bears are gold's strongest case: +95% through 2020-23, +64% through Volcker.

title: Which structural grower explains gold's drift? — anchor study for the model intercept (chartpack)
desc: Quarterly 1971-2026: gold's +8.4%/yr drift vs eight candidate anchors. Federal debt / total financial assets / total debt / monetary base match the drift (7.6-8.4%/yr); CPI and GDP undershoot. Cointegration table quantifies the levels-space small-n problem (half-lives 6-70y = 0.4-4.4 independent episodes; only M2 clears). 150-year JST view: the peg absorbs money growth pre-1971, then releases it in jumps.

title: Gold & Bitcoin CMA — 10-slide evidence deck (lit review → model selection → regressions → portfolio role)
desc: Ten slides: 19 papers + 17 shops collapse into 7 approach families; why returns-space gold and a gold-tethered BTC; the simple vs sophisticated regression with stars and OOS tests vs a random walk; the ~10-12%/yr official-sector intercept; BTC share scenarios; gold's extreme-event portfolio role (inflation-threshold and drawdown-depth sensitivity tables) and the 60/40 sleeve competition vs TIPS/commodities. Every number scripted.

title: Gold Factor-Regression Model — returns-space, rolling 60-month, OOS vs random walk
desc: Gold (LBMA) log-returns regressed on macro factor changes (DXY, 10Y TIPS real, 10Y breakeven, WTI, VIX, MOVE, S&P, US Agg bonds). Two pages: In-sample and Out-of-sample (estimate beta on trailing 60 months -> apply to next period's macros). Interactive variable selection auto-extends history (full model 2003 TIPS wall; drop TIPS -> 1990/1986). Best-subset presets, Diebold-Mariano vs random walk (beats RW daily/weekly/monthly), walk-forward selection, residual diagnostics. Live interactive dashboard (self-contained).

title: Gold Factor Model — Excel (formula-driven + Bloomberg BDH)
desc: Generic daily factor-regression template: paste a Date column, a dependent series (Y), and up to 9 explanatory series; set each column transform (log return / Δlevel) and a Monthly/Weekly/Quarterly toggle. Live LINEST static regression + 5y rolling walk-forward OOS + charts, plus a Diagnostics tab that self-checks the paste. Robust period key (no array constants). Tested vs numpy across all 3 frequencies.

title: BTC ETF ownership — long-only ownership, relative (graph 1 of 3)
desc: Interactive: long-only ownership as a % of shares outstanding, RELATIVE across asset classes — 3 Bitcoin ETFs vs 5 gold ETFs vs 4 equity-index ETFs (SPY/IVV/QQQ/IWM) vs S&P mid-cap and small-cap stock means. From SEC Form 13F bulk data (period 2026-03-31). Gradient: Bitcoin ~10% < Gold ~24% < Equity-index ~28% < stocks ~65%.

title: BTC ETF ownership — institutional base composition (graph 2 of 3)
desc: Interactive stacked bars: 13F institutional base by investor type (passive index / active long-only / pension-insurance-wealth / hedge fund / market maker / bank-dealer), % of shares outstanding, for Bitcoin vs gold vs equity-index ETF means + stock means. Bitcoin ETFs are hedge-fund/basis-trade skewed (IBIT hedge funds ~= all long-only); gold ETFs are clean real-money (~0.4% hedge funds).

title: BTC ETF ownership — long-only funds' actual allocation (graph 3 of 3)
desc: Interactive: of the long-only funds identified, what bitcoin/gold/equity-index ETFs represent as a % of their TOTAL 13F book (full per-manager pass over the bulk data). Headline: long-only managers hold ~0.02% of book in bitcoin ETFs vs ~0.13% in gold — ~7x more gold than bitcoin; 23% hold any bitcoin ETF vs 47% gold. Even active managers: 0.02% bitcoin.

title: Gold CMA — what drives it: papers & shops × price factors × approach families (interactive map)
desc: Interactive relationship map behind the gold capital-market assumption. Center column = every major source from our gold-CMA literature review (19 academic papers + 17 industry shops). Lines LEFT connect each source to the price factors it claims move gold (20 elements: real rates, DXY, a buyer-weighted FX basket, inflation swaps, MOVE, M2, central-bank demand, de-dollarization, geopolitical risk, supply, etc.); lines RIGHT connect it to its modeling approach (7 MECE families: historical-average, zero-real/Golden-Constant, real-rate+USD factor model, monetary/M2-debasement, trend+mean-reversion/regime-switching, official-sector/de-dollarization, supply-demand/wealth-share). Hover any node to trace its links; click to pin. Self-contained, no dependencies.
